At the request of the parties, the Commission permitted them to file their respective written submissions, if any, within four weeks, and the matter was reserved for orders. - a) On 19.04.2021, the Hon’ble Supreme Court issued the _2021 SC GIB Order_ . By way of the said email, the Petitioner provided the documents in support of its claim arising from the above-mentioned Change in Law events. The physical copies of the supporting documents were also dispatched to NHPC for verification and reconciliation of the change-in-law claims. - t) Accordingly, the Petitioner is filing the instant petition seeking relief on account of the occurrence of the aforementioned Change in Law events. - j) The Petitioner has submitted that the above events have already been recognised as ‘Change in Law’ events by the Commission vide its order dated 11.05.2024 in petition no. 381/MP/2023 (filed by M/s Altra Xergi Power Private Limited in respect of 380MW solar power project, wherein NHPC acts as an intermediary procurer). 14. In view of the above, we are of the view that the cause of action starts from 18.07.2022, i.e., the date of ratification by the Members of the SC Committee. We further observe that the project was fully commissioned on 10.12.2022, whereas the petition was filed on 03.09.2024. As such, we are of the view that the petition was filed within time and the change in law claim qua _2021 SC GIB Order_ is not barred by limitation under the Limitation Act, 1963. - (ii) _**the Petitioner has categorically waived its right to raise the Change in Law claim by executing the Affidavit/Supplementary Affidavit; And**_ _and the Commission may consider the approval of the procurement of power as sought in the petition accordingly._ _**68. It is in the above context that we accept that the regulatory powers of the Central Commission ought to have been properly exercised to do complete justice to the claims for compensation it having been denied by depriving the SPPDs of their legitimate expectation of relief vis-à-vis the burden of carrying cost as well, rendering the dispensation partially unfair._ _“Pending further orders, the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) shall comply with the directions issued in paragraph 109 of the impugned order dated 15 September 2022 of the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity. The contracting parties are to carry out reconciliation on account of additional expenditure as per Article 12 of the PPA by exhibiting a clear and one-to-one correlation between the project and the invoices raised, supported with an auditor certificate on account of the _2021 GST Notification_ and the _2021 SC GIB Order_ . - e) The directions issued in this Order so far as they relate to compensation for the period post Commercial Operation Date of the projects in question as also towards carrying cost (pre-COD & post-COD) shall not be enforced and shall be subject to further orders of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. 8880/2022 in _Telangana Northern Power Distribution Company Limited & Anr.
